alternatives.action: Reuse the current v2 rule unchanged and make producer/consumer launch contexts canonical byte-for-byte, including script-entrypoint and PYTHONPATH spellings.
alternatives.benefit: No new mechanism or generation schema; strict fail-closed response; the same-context actual HTTP producer/reader compatibility has now passed.
alternatives.cost_and_migration: A harmless entrypoint path change invalidates vector use and forces typed text fallback even when all selected modules, source, model and encoder bytes are unchanged. Every deployment and job must share an identical canonical path list. No schema migration, but path coordination is operationally load-bearing.
alternatives.risk: Conservatism protects against path changes but does not hash the contents of every existing sys.path directory or prove all lazy import resolution.
alternatives.status_authority_time: No external authority or time claim is introduced. Runtime identity remains a candidate executable-material predicate only.

alternatives.action: Extend the existing owner to a versioned v3 material basis. Reuse _SOURCE_FILES, the recursive installed distribution file closure, nine-file model manifest/member hashes, actual loaded asset identity and actual encoder fingerprint. Replace literal whole-sys.path equality with a typed selected-module resolution witness: actual loaded origin and bytes, distribution/file ownership where available, and a first-effective-resolution check for the model/encoder/required runtime modules. Bind interpreter/ABI and relevant import controls. Keep fail-closed for missing files, non-file loaders, ambiguous namespace packages, unsupported meta_path finders, or unverifiable first-hit resolution.
alternatives.benefit: Different launcher/script directories can share one basis only when they resolve the exact same selected code/material; real selected shadows still change origin/content or fail resolution proof.
alternatives.cost_and_migration: New typed module/provenance schema and adversarial importer tests are required. The current v2 generation cannot be silently reinterpreted as v3: either retain an explicit v2 reader with exact-path semantics or regenerate/reissue selected generations under v3. Consumer/API intent DTO shape can remain unchanged; only rule identity and source-owned material owner change.
alternatives.risk: A naive omission of sys.path is unsafe: it could miss imports from an unbound path. Resolution evidence must be generic enough to cover the modules used by actual encoder/model code; unsupported dynamics must refuse.
alternatives.status_authority_time: Still internal technical material identity. It cannot certify package provenance beyond the recorded local distribution bytes, production currentness, legal truth, issuer authority or custody.

alternatives.action: No standalone consolidation is required now: current runtime digest, source digest, encoder fingerprint, model digest and final binding are already centralized in one source-owned owner and lease.
alternatives.benefit: Avoids duplicate material ledgers or parallel cache identities.
alternatives.cost_and_migration: If B is chosen, add its selected resolution proof to that same owner/binding rather than a second independent authority object.

alternatives.action: If importlib/metadata cannot produce a generic, behaviorally verified first-hit proof within the existing owner, build only a small typed import-resolution component and let the existing Legal owner compose it.
alternatives.benefit: Creates a dedicated owner for import provenance only when existing primitives cannot express the needed proof.
alternatives.cost_and_migration: Additional component, tests and rule-version migration; avoid a new general runtime registry or broad architecture unless a concrete unsupported import case requires it.

author_recommendation: Keep current v2 execution and artifact semantics unchanged while G records the equality choice. A is a defensible conservative contract only if canonical producer/consumer launch profiles are operationally acceptable. B remains conditional on cross-entrypoint portability being a product requirement and G accepting the broader source-bound import-resolution falsifiers. Do not locally weaken v2 before that choice.
